features.title: State layer as startup anchor
features.behavior: Cold-start for cross-module and resume tasks begins with current-status, current-sprint and release-status before local search.

verification.target: Read docs/current-status.md, docs/current-sprint.md and docs/release-status.md before local search.

features.residual_risk: State docs still need manual updates after each non-trivial task.

features.title: Lifecycle with focused validation
features.behavior: Each non-trivial task must record a local hypothesis, make a bounded edit and immediately run focused validation before widening scope.

verification.target: Use the lifecycle flow and confirm that the first post-edit action is a focused validation step.

features.residual_risk: Discipline is enforced by process and review, not by a runtime hook yet.

features.title: Task routing by mode
features.behavior: Research, implementation, review and release tasks are routed through explicit modes with different tool and output expectations.

verification.target: Classify the task against docs/agent-routing-matrix.md before expanding scope.

features.residual_risk: Routing still depends on operator discipline for ambiguous tasks.

features.title: Synthetic and real-folder end-to-end validation
features.behavior: Cross-module converter changes are verified through schema-backed run-package validation and end-to-end runs, not only unit tests.
features.residual_risk: Real-corpus E2E still requires a deliberate task decision and is not part of every CI run.

features.title: Machine-readable harness feature spine
features.behavior: Harness capabilities are tracked in a machine-readable file with behavior, state, verification and evidence instead of relying on narrative roadmap alone.
features.residual_risk: The spine currently covers the harness layer and not every product capability of the converter.

features.title: Bootstrap contract for cold start
features.behavior: A new session can reacquire the repo, environment, release scope and next validation path without broad search.
features.residual_risk: Bootstrap still depends on a healthy local .venv and Windows OCR prerequisites.

features.title: Clean exit checklist
features.behavior: Every non-trivial task ends with validation evidence, state updates, residual risk capture and resume breadcrumbs.
features.residual_risk: Checklist enforcement is procedural until a higher-level workflow hook is added.

features.title: Sprint contract template
features.behavior: Non-trivial tasks can declare goal, non-goals, local hypothesis, validation plan and stop conditions before edits begin.
features.residual_risk: The template exists, but adoption still depends on task complexity and operator judgment.

features.title: Evaluator rubric for completion quality
features.behavior: Task quality can be scored against scope control, validation, evidence and closeout instead of relying on subjective completion claims.
features.residual_risk: The rubric is defined and now feeds a generated weekly snapshot, but final qualitative judgement still needs human review.

features.title: Harness assets validator in CI
features.behavior: Core harness artifacts are validated in CI so regressions in feature spine or required process docs fail early.
features.residual_risk: The validator checks structure and file presence, not the semantic quality of every document.

features.title: Canonical document.v1 package
features.behavior: The main product output is a portable document.v1.json package with source metadata, processing route, semantic metadata, structural units, assets and quality flags instead of plain text only, plus root-level processed-documents-catalog JSON/XLSX indexes that map source names to output folders, statuses and operator hyperlinks, and first-class human-readable Markdown/HTML exports for operator QC.
features.residual_risk: Advanced PDF tables, formulas and figures now have heuristic unit extraction, but pixel-perfect table geometry and multimodal figure understanding remain downstream concerns.

features.title: DOCX native conversion route
features.behavior: DOCX files are processed natively with reading-order preservation, semantic units for headings, lists, captions, tables, formulas, headers, footers and footnotes, extracted media assets and search_text.txt.
features.residual_risk: DOCX headers, footers, footnotes and formulas are extracted heuristically from package XML; complex field codes and linked external objects may still need review.

features.title: PDF text-layer conversion route
features.behavior: PDF files with an extractable text layer are processed without OCR using layout-first extraction, page provenance, repeated edge-block filtering into header/footer units and heuristic table/formula/figure unit extraction.
features.residual_risk: PDF table/formula/figure extraction is heuristic over text blocks; exact cell geometry, figure pixels and multimodal semantics remain downstream/review concerns.

features.title: PDF scan OCR route
features.behavior: PDF scans are processed through OCR into searchable.pdf and sidecar text, then emitted into canonical document packages with OCR provenance, quality flags and heuristic table/formula/figure units from OCR text.
features.residual_risk: Optional OCR helpers jbig2, pngquant and verapdf are not required and remain uninstalled by default.

features.title: XLSX native conversion route
features.behavior: XLSX workbooks are processed natively with worksheet sections, inferred sheet tables, row and cell units, structured cell payloads, preserved Excel formulas and cached formula values where present.
features.residual_risk: The converter preserves Excel formulas and cached workbook values but does not recalculate formulas; downstream calculation still needs an Excel-compatible formula engine or recalculation step.

features.title: Formula recognition provider env config
features.behavior: Converter runtime auto-loads formula recognition provider, model and API key from `.env.local`/`.env` plus process environment overrides, supporting both explicit `FORMULA_RECOGNITION_*` keys and shorthand aliases like `LLM_PROVIDER`, provider-specific model keys and `FORMULA_MODEL`, while run metadata stores only provider/model/configured and never serializes the secret itself.
features.residual_risk: The env loader searches the current working directory and its ancestors; if the converter is launched from an unrelated directory, the operator must export the variables explicitly or start the command from the project tree. Only the formula-recognition slice is consumed so far; the generic non-formula `OPENROUTER_MODEL` is currently a fallback alias, not an independently used runtime setting elsewhere in the converter.

features.title: Formula image recognition postprocess
features.behavior: When formula recognition is configured, runner reopens each canonical `document.v1.json`, scans `formula_image` units, first tries local WMF/MathType hint extraction and then falls back to an OpenRouter multimodal call for unresolved assets, writing successful results back into `unit.text`, `unit.formula`, `processing.formula_recognition` and a sidecar `formula-recognition.jsonl` artifact.
features.residual_risk: Automated validation uses mocked provider responses and does not spend real OpenRouter credits; live quality still depends on provider availability, model behavior and successful rasterization of WMF/EMF assets on Windows.

features.title: Semantic document metadata block
features.behavior: Each canonical package includes rule-based title, document_type, short_summary, confidence and method fields without depending on an external LLM.
features.residual_risk: Rule-based classification still depends on corpus wording and may need new patterns on unseen document families.

features.title: Quality flags and review-required reporting
features.behavior: The converter emits normalized document and unit quality flags, review-required.jsonl, root-level processed-documents-catalog JSON/XLSX indexes and summary reason buckets for failed, partial and review-required cases.
features.residual_risk: Some quality signals remain heuristic and may need threshold tuning on new corpora.

features.title: Resume, dedup and queue-state reuse
features.behavior: Repeated runs reuse previous output for unchanged files, preserve duplicate provenance and keep queue-state stable instead of reprocessing blindly.
features.residual_risk: Resume behavior is validated within current local run layout and has not been generalized to distributed execution.

features.title: Chunking and downstream handoff
features.behavior: Structural units can be transformed into portability-safe chunks.v1.jsonl and handed downstream without re-running OCR or reparsing the source files.
features.residual_risk: DB mapping notes and downstream loaders still evolve separately from the converter runtime.

features.title: Operator GUI and Windows release packaging
features.behavior: Operators can run the converter through a GUI with progress, current file, cancel, open output, HTML QC and summary counts, while Windows packaging produces a portable EXE and release zip.
features.residual_risk: Pause and resume are intentionally not exposed as GUI controls; the product relies on safe rerun semantics instead.

features.title: Machine-readable telemetry companion
features.behavior: Task-level validation and state-update signals are stored in a schema-backed JSONL companion with feature traceability, alongside the human-readable markdown telemetry log.
features.residual_risk: Historical telemetry remains primarily in markdown; JSONL starts as a structured companion from the latest harness iterations.

features.title: Machine-readable quality scorecard companion
features.behavior: Observed quality signals are summarized from structured telemetry and feature spine into a schema-backed scorecard companion, while the human-readable markdown structured companion section is kept in sync through a generated markdown check and can be consumed by the weekly eval loop.
features.residual_risk: Generated scores and markdown sync are proxy signals from telemetry coverage and still need qualitative interpretation in the weekly eval loop.

features.title: Generated weekly eval companion
features.behavior: Weekly eval can be refreshed in one command or via an optional Windows Scheduled Task helper from the machine-readable scorecard, structured telemetry and machine-readable sampled weekly reviews into generated JSON and markdown snapshots with coverage gaps, next actions and qualitative sampling evidence.
features.residual_risk: Weekly snapshot больше не purely proxy-only на reviewed weeks; schedule helper removes refresh overhead, but qualitative review scores in docs/agent-weekly-reviews.v1.json still require human/agent sampling discipline.
